name: Brittany

attributes.attribute: an ancient Celtic land now forming much of France
a land brought under Roman rule
in Breton the name is Breizh, and the western part stayed heavily Breton-speaking until the twentieth century

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Brittany is a land that faces the Atlantic on the Celtic fringe of France. The Breton speakers call the region Breizh. The western half, Breizh-Izel or Lower Brittany, was largely Breton in speech and way. The decline of the spoken tongue came fast in the twentieth century. The eastern half, Upper Brittany, is home to the cities of Nantes and Rennes. In those towns the near tongue is a Gallic dialect called Gallo, with a touch of Breton. In this book the name Brittany also points the reader toward the entry for GAUL.

okr.objective: Portray Brittany as a Celtic Atlantic land, its west a Breizh stronghold and its east home of French.
